notes.title: Developer Diary #6 - Combat
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

Last month, we introduced some of the weapons and the four melee combat styles you can experience. This month, we will show you the main types of player movements you get to use in the game and how the combat has grown through the game’s development in Morbid: The Lords of Ire. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

General Combat
In Morbid: The Lords of Ire, combat is fluid like a dance - by keeping active, you can get the most out of combat and kill more enemies with ease. By timing your blocks and attacks, you are able to reserve more stamina and fare better in your battle against evil. 

Basic Attacks
Swing your weapon to perform a range of combo attacks. Combos are different depending on your weapon class and wielding style. 

Rage Breaker
When an enemy becomes Enraged it cannot be staggered. When you encounter a raged enemy, perform a Rage Breaker attack to break through before they regain their posture.

Riposte
When an enemy hit is about to land on you, parry the strike and perform a brutal counterattack. It is important to keep in mind that some powerful attacks cannot be parried.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/534005715f8bcb2c1dd59f8b6511bca696a71a4c.gif
Perfect Block
It is important to note that, while blocking, your stamina regenerates at a slower rate. However, perfectly timed blocks restore Stamina, impact enemy Posture, and also rebound most projectiles.

Critical Blow 
Once enemy posture is gone, you can perform a Critical Blow on the staggered foe.
This deals enormous amounts of damage and is often lethal. This move also fully restores the Striver’s stamina bar. In some situations, you may choose to use the Spectre Blaser instead to deliver the Critical Blow.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/1cf3100f9dbcfe33acf1f6da8369baf54bb046d6.gif

Sneaking and Backstab
Sneaking allows the player to approach tougher encounters discreetly, and possibly gain the upper hand with a powerful backstab. A successful backstab takes away a lot of posture and health, and in some cases, when the posture is fully drained, it outright kills the enemy on a single hit.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/31a616070ad06c7985fa8bb08b52eca685c72de2.gif

Spectre Blaster
The Spectre Blaster is attuned for staggering foes, rather than dealing damage. It is a supporting tool for melee combat with which one can interrupt dangerous attacks. The Spectre Blaster holds a single slug and can be reloaded by slaying an enemy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/69ef6f00c38575dfc64ff0fa1545740eb1f2b621.gif

Dash
Dash allows you to make a quick evasive move in any direction. This move is good for dodging smaller attacks and gaining an advantage during combat as it uses less of the Striver’s stamina.

Dodge Roll
Perform a Dodge Roll to avoid larger attacks. The player is invulnerable while dodge rolling, and although you can dodge a greater distance, it will cost you more stamina.

Lunge Attack 
This move is earned separately through a Blessing. You can Lunge Attack from a dodge roll, which allows for the evasive manoeuvre to be used as an offensive move.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

We have come a long way since our previous release, Morbid: The Seven Acolytes, and want to thank everyone who has played the demo and given us feedback, which we are constantly reading through. 

Whilst we appreciate all the souls-like fans, it’s important to note that we’re not trying to represent a souls-like game but a more fast-paced hack-and-slash action game with souls-like elements. Morbid: The Lords of Ire is continuously under development and we will keep making the combat in our game the best it can be!

And lastly, we thought we’d show you some behind-the-scenes shots of the motion captures taken by the developers at the Still Running studio. Almost every animation you see in-game is created in real life using motion capture (and yes, that is the CEO of Still Running stumbling around)...enjoy!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/8275d9b9d3569e2cdd54da216b5f7cdb2c32b351.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/85432a954fd42bb1a889b50f79dadf72286f1ced.gif
One of the first motion captures we ever did for Morbid: The Lords of Ire (Cosmian Reborn enemy)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/a9386ee4c9a7b2e6ec79f3d092f0507b7a87f00a.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b18fa56ba40904dcf253f8027aaca7045766c85d.gif
Another early motion capture session for the Tusker Champion enemy

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/7c5467f0a883f0c817391c6c320617363fc37923.png
Having fun with Battle Brute (props are important!)


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

notes.title: Developer Diary #5 - Weapons
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

This month, we would like to show you just some of the gut-wrenching and powerful weapons that you will find in Morbid: The Lords of Ire. Which will you choose to slaughter the hideous creatures that await your path? 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png


Sword of Dibrom

The Sword of Dibrom is a legendary sword that the Striver is allotted at the beginning of her gruesome journey. Every Striver receives the sword when they first begin their training. It is a fine sword and has served the Striver well through many dire scenarios. Though its power has waned over the years, the blade still reminds her of the path she has hitherto fared.

“The sword still reminds you of the path you've hitherto fared. Its warm hilt has guided you through the cursed hamlet of Solya, the murky streets of Yortael, the putrid Felfields, and the deadly maze that was Grimwald's Grove.

By its trusty blade, many a mighty foe has fallen, the mindless Boatswain Borga, the legless witch Yaga Moer, the formidable Undead Mammoth-Beast, and of course, the Seven Acolytes of Mornia.”

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/0fb045e5add6b66042a62ffe0d0976752e578afd.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/c86c9b07944cabbcb4a962808e320304955713aa.png
The Sword of Dibrom is a legendary sword that the Striver is allotted at the beginning of her gruesome journey. 


Mountain’s Edge

Great axes trade away speed for high damage and impact. Most designs thus endorse a barbaric style of combat where ferocity reigns and grace matters not. Those who favor the brutish way of the great axe often declare that in battle elegance is irrelevant; only the results matter. One could say they are not wrong.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/829bcd85eeee1b4dd0f388fcd696b81abc2b30a1.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b7bd6786a969a7b0a95496a49a8127abb14fb155.png
Mountain’s Edge is a Two-Handed executioner's Great Axe of Rimeholdian origin, named after the mountain itself.


Fists of Ire

Knuckle dusters have historically been a popular weapon class among the martial artists of Ire. Various designs and materials have been used in making these so-called, iron fists. Though low in damage across the board, they all share one distinguishing feature; they provide the combattant with superior control over their maneuvers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/f78f7b4079cc65ee68042f68e987e549d75fb7a0.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/4babe2061299e4a72180a7a810aaededaa20593c.png
Fists of Ire are Iron fists forged in Irelia and are part of the capital's own high-quality weapon family. 


Flensing Daggers

Daggers allow for a combat rhythm of unparalleled rapidity. No other weapon class can match the speed with which a combatant armed with two deadly dirks can take on an enemy. However, the swift moves are being paid for in diminished damage and impact, as small blades create small wounds and carry little inertia.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/4f2f3445c06a410f4e4bbf259255c43dafb25207.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/07b76bb398f2704bfb6cfb91d373f97f799d1b21.png
Flensing Daggers are from Dunghaven, historically used by the fishermen of yore for flensing their catch.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

notes.title: Developer Diary #4 - Blessings
notes.content:
Yuletide Blessings to you, Striver!

We hope that you have all had a festive and merry Yuletide season! As an extra little gift, we're here to bring you a sneak peak into the Blessings feature in Morbid: The Lords of Ire.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

Similarly to Morbid: The Seven Acolytes, the Blessings in Morbid: The Lords of Ire allows the player to build their character by levelling up and customising the skillset of the Striver in even more varied and tangible ways.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/ebbd583ce858c228b101db0bd935c0859a5fb327.png

The Blessings can be found one by one as you progress through the game and find artifacts (Tomes of Insight) which you return to Yan, the Blessed One, in the Hall of Redemption to be deciphered.
Yan also allows you to upgrade tiers and buy more slots for your Blessings using Skill Points. There are maximum of three Blessing Slots, each upgradeable up to level three.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

Blessing of the Healer

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/3b87d817eaea66b3742daf7e0d4788a6a0e5a132.png
*Blessing Card Concept Art

Blessing of the Healer gifts the player with a larger Health Bar.
With higher Tiers, it will improve healing effects and give the player another life.

Blessing of the Acrobat

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/19e75ee0e9c31d795063a75777dca3c0446e4f1b.png
*Blessing Card Concept Art

Blessing of the Acrobat gifts the player a larger Stamina Bar.
With higher Tiers it regenerates Stamina faster and removes Stamina downtime.

Blessing of the Gunslinger

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/ae4e1199dfc302eb7b45550f46aec54bb55ec19b.png
*Blessing Card Concept Art

Blessing of the Gunslinger gifts the player with shots that have more impact.
With higher Tiers the player obtains Piercing Bullets and doubles the Ammo cap.

These 3 Blessings are just some of what you will get to experience in Morbid: The Lords of Ire, and there will be many more unique and useful Blessings to come in the full game!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

notes.title: Developer Diary #3 - Environments
notes.content:
Greetings, Striver!

The land of Ire has been divided into five realms, governed by the five factions and led by the five Acolyte leaders - 'The Lords of Ire'.

In Morbid: The Lords of Ire, you must battle your way through these realms, facing horrid monstrosities, special encounters and quests. Ultimately, one by one, it is your goal to defeat the five Acolyte lords.

Get a taste of the stricken land of Ire by checking out just some of the environments you will battle across, in hopes of freeing from the evil grip of the Gahars, below...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

RIMEHOLD

"For ages, the stoic warriors of Rimehold were the noble watchmen of the Wintry Mountains. With pride and vigilance, they guarded the mountain passage between Mornia and Ire."

Often referred to as 'The Wintry Mountains', this snowbound realm is one of the first gruesome lands that you will visit in this action-adventure.

Tread through deep snowy passes and explore frozen stone strongholds in Rimehold, home to the forever-doomed living and dead accursed warriors.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/8a6ae3a66e3822a26c680915fd112f78abebf5da.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/689712b84b4d5281c10e2c47cd2598fa755c7ff6.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/53f8ef5c2a008fb118bd6bbcd3f1470a8170a90d.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

IRELIA

"As the onslaught continued, most Irelians fled the city, but some refused to flee. Those who stayed split into two factions: Some tried to defend the city against the insect invaders, while others chose not to fight but to worship the monstrosities as their new overlords."

The monumental capital of Ire, Irelia fell into ruin when a colony of parasitic insect demons invaded the city.

Ruled by the Cult of Culex, an evil communion, Irelia features towering citadels and gothic-Victorian architecture. Away from the blood-drenched streets, players can also explore the Rejectorium - the orphanage of Irelia.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/e6eda5ee411f7c01d31d58d13444e44a81694225.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b1013ead66887fb8538f12f516f8bd5af8e84b82.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b8eafe6893f892a787a32feed292337c083b9684.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

HALL OF REDEMPTION

"You made it back, Striver! What news from Rimehold? …So—it is as I feared. The great corruptors are among us once more. The Gahars have returned."

Formerly known as the Cathedral of Wrath, the Hall of Redemption is the commemorative hall where the last Striver defeated Inquisitor Odius and Redeemed Mornia in Morbid: The Seven Acolytes.

Players will be able to use the Hall of Redemption as a hub to upgrade their abilities and equipment, or seek shelter from the morbid world outside.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/d52141d2af44a91c244c1e45096a08789403dbca.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/b882a0b1bc65d6dbb459078fa7c474ea04bc2dc9.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/e774bfd3a57ca84b517bcd339fc61bce6142c156.png
All in-game images are still work-in-progress, and may change before release!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/fc10c018df5c11cd7f3ec42bac8db710827e360d.png

Be wary, Striver, for there are more gruesome Realms that await you in Morbid: The Lords of Ire...

notes.title: Developer Diary #1 - The Striver
notes.content:
"By redeeming Mornia, and liberating the kingdom from under the sway of the Gahars and their Acolytes, the last Striver of Dibrom so completed her sacred mission. But while her mission ended, her duty resumed, for even with all the Acolytes slain, the Gahars themselves never truly died."

As you may have seen from our new store capsule imagery, The Striver has become a much bigger focus of Morbid: The Lords of Ire, as the Morbid franchise shifts from 2D pixel-art to 3D immersion.

The brand-new featured art from the team at Still Running gives us our first detailed look at our fearless protagonist, Striver.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/79932700cd360b67b66ab1560650148101c7de2d.png

Players of Morbid: The Seven Acolytes will recognise our main protagonist of the game's sequel, Morbid: The Lords of Ire. Years after defeating the Seven Acolytes and liberating the kingdom of Mornia from evil, Striver returns as duty calls upon her once more, as another set of abysmal Acolytes await to be slain.

In Morbid: The Lords of Ire, players will be able to "Become The Striver", taking control of the gutsy heroine and experiencing a visceral 3D world in third-person view. We can't wait for players to step into the shoes of The Last Striver of Dibrom and explore the gore-fueled worlds that await you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43609920/418522e596642f8217a35ee2c6b428d226a1fb93.png

notes.title: Update 5 - Morbid Rebirth
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We have another exciting update for you today!

Update 5 is now live and birngs two much requested features to Morbid: The Seven Acolytes!

Update 5 changes

 Map Feature added
 New Game Plus added


Map

We know you've been wanting a map so we're very pleased to deliver it! Here's an image of what it looks like in the starting area in-game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38037977/ca3b989fa44fd32b8ed0804ad5bfc0ec847d6b5a.jpg

New Game Plus

If you have completed the core campaign of Morbid, you now have the opportunity to start New Game Plus and go back and challenge The Seven Acolytes for a new harder experience. 

The New Game Plus features consecutive additive difficulty. Each time you beat the campaign you can go back to continue to challenge them for a tougher and tougher experience!

To start New Game Plus load a save slot that has beaten the campaign and it will prompt you to find a new option in the shrine. 

Join your fellow Strivers on Discord.

notes.title: Update 3!
notes.content:
Hi all,

We have a new content update that we want to share with you which focuses on some quality of life improvements to the game. 

*Edit - updated to include Korean and Traditional Chinese language support.

Please find all the details below;

Tutorial

Incorrect button prompt in one of the tutorials' is fixed

Bosses

Lorn's AI fixed, pathfinding fixed and hitboxes fixed

Font

Total amount of fonts has been reduced from 5 to 2. This will lower the loading time between language changes by around 50%

Enemy

Lorn's combo attack hitboxes are fixed
FloraSoul's attack hitboxes are fixed

Weapon

Fist weapons now have longer distance where they "leap" towards the enemy
Mecha Gloves has been nerfed

Player

Hey Everyone!

Change list:
|PARRY| - Doing a parry attack makes the player invulnerable for the period of the attack
|PARRY| - Parry engages faster
|PARRY| - Parry delay after being hit / interrupted is reduced
|PARRY| - A "failed" parry no longer does damage to the player
|PARRY| - Blocking in a direction other than the current movement direction is now easier 
|PARRY| - Blocking now faces the correct direction when playing with keyboard + mouse
|PLAYER| - Moving speed (walking and running) has been increased. 
|PLAYER| - Running uses less stamina 
|PLAYER| - Players hitbox is a bit more forgiving
|PLAYER| - Changing load-outs in-game is now possible (Q on keyboard, or RB/R1 on gamepad)
|INVENTORY| - Mouse support has been added to the inventory
|OPTIONS| - Added option for changing the strength of the gamepad vibration

Thank you to those who has raised these issues and brought them to our attention. We hope these changes improve your Morbid experience.

Enjoy!

notes.title: A word from the developer
notes.content:
Hello everyone, this is Santeri Relander here. I'm the main coder and CEO of Still Running, among other things.

Some of you may have already noticed that I've been replying to the reviews, and forum post's actively. This is what I've always done, ever since I released my first game on Android back in 2013. I feel that engaging with the community is very important, and to make yourself available for any questions and issues that may rise. (I actually very much enjoy talking about a game I've worked on with other people!)

Right now however, I feel overwhelmed. I didn't expect so much attention for the game, and I think I'm going to need to take a couple of days just to focus on the game itself.

A bit of backstory

We've been working on Morbid for almost two years now. We currently have three very talented artist's at Still Running, one of which is also our level designer. We also have our amazing composer here, who's doubling up as our writer. We've all worked long days with the game. Pretty much your basic indie studio. Sweat, tears, blood and all that. They've all done an amazing job with the game, and I couldn't be more proud of the people I work with every day.

However, as for the coding. That's a bit of a different story. The project was originally supposed to be done within 12 months, and it was planned for atleast two full-time coders. Unfortunately, I ended up writing about 90% of the code there is in Morbid.

I was responsible for porting the game to Switch/PS4/Xbox, the player, most enemies, creating the pathfinding to the enemies, shadow system, lighting engine, menu's, blessings screen, UI, EditMode (a tool which others used to place all items and enemies etc), audio engine, collision system, system for breakable assets, blood (which there is a-lot of), menagerie, end credits, profile handling, gamepad handling, loading screens (there's a surprising amount of work on making a loading screen to a game, and to make it load as fast as possible)... You get the point.

Near the end of those 12 months, I realized I wouldn’t be able to make it. I explained the situation to our publisher, and asked for more time. They understood the situation, and wanted to make the game the best it can be. We got more time.

2019 and 2020 have been the most stressful years of my entire life, as there was quite a-lot happening in my personal life as well. So, I was hoping that once the game was out, I would've had the time to relax a little. (We actually never even had a launch party, as we got an alert for possible Corona contamination at the office)

Sounds like an excuse to me...

Right, sorry. I got side tracked...

I wanted to apologize, as only now I understand the expectations for a game like this and I'm sorry I wasn't able to quite meet them. Working on something for so long got me blind for my own work. I can now see quite a few things I want to improve on, such as the stamina, player speed, combat, and parrying. I’ll start working on these, among other things, and you guys should be getting a patch by the end of this week.

As for rebindable keys, ultra-wide support, storage box and such, I hear you. These I’ll work on as soon as possible.

Thank you for understanding, and thank you for reading through my wall of text,


Santeri
